chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us saying: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated to us from 'Asim ibn Hamid, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
When a person is placed in his grave, two angels come to him, one from his right and one from his left, and Satan is made to stand before him, his eyes like copper.
Then he is asked: 'What do you say about this man who was among you?'
He is overwhelmed by fear; if he is a believer, he says: 'Are you asking me about Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?'
They say to him: 'Yes,' a sleep with no dream in it.
And his grave is widened for him by nine cubits.
Then he sees his place in Paradise.
And that is the word of Allah, the Almighty: 'Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in this life and in the Hereafter.'
If he is a disbeliever, they say to him: 'What is this man who came among you?'
So they leave him alone with Satan.

key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ: before him / in front of him

ai.seo_question: What happens to the believer and the disbeliever in the grave after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* details the post-mortem interrogation by two angels and Satan, highlighting the believer's confident affirmation of Muhammad's (peace be upon him and his family) prophethood as the 'firm word' (al-Qawl al-Thabit). The text explicitly links this theological certainty to the Quranic promise of a spacious grave and a glimpse of Paradise, contrasting it with the disbeliever's confusion and isolation with Satan. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the centrality of the Prophet's lineage and truth in securing the soul's comfort during the intermediate state (Barzakh).
